bear.argument: Meta is a risky investment on the filing's own numbers. Reality Labs reduced 2025 operating profit by about $19.19 billion, and management expects 2026 RL operating losses to remain similar. Net income fell from $62.36 billion in 2024 to $60.46 billion in 2025, and the effective tax rate rose to 30% from 12%, partly due to a valuation allowance charge tied to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Capital spending is climbing, with 2026 capex guided to $115 to $135 billion, so the cash returned to shareholders must compete with heavy infrastructure and AI commitments. Substantially all revenue comes from advertising, and the filing says platform and regulatory developments will continue to hurt ad revenue for the foreseeable future. The European subscription-for-no-ads dispute could force a materially worse experience for European users. Public shareholders also have limited influence, since the founder and CEO controls a majority of the voting power.

claims.claim: Reality Labs losses are large and expected to persist
claims.quote: our investments in Reality Labs reduced our 2025 overall operating profit by approximately $19.19 billion, and we expect our 2026 Reality Labs operating losses to remain similar to 2025

claims.claim: Capital spending is set to rise sharply, pressuring free cash flow
claims.quote: We anticipate making capital expenditures of approximately $115 billion to $135 billion in 2026 to support our AI efforts and core business

claims.claim: Advertising faces continuing adverse effects from data and platform limits
claims.quote: the legislative, regulatory and platform developments described above will continue to adversely impact our advertising revenue for the foreseeable future

claims.claim: Controlling shareholder limits public shareholders' influence
claims.quote: Holders of our Class B common stock, including our founder, Chairman, and CEO, together hold a majority of the combined voting power of our outstanding capital stock

bull.argument: Meta's filing shows a business that is growing fast and converting that growth into cash. Total 2025 revenue rose 22% to $200.97 billion, with advertising revenue up 22% on 12% higher ad impressions and a 9% higher average price per ad. Income from operations grew 20% to $83.28 billion, and Family of Apps operating margin was 52%. Operating cash flow reached $115.80 billion, and the company returned $31.57 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends. The opponent is right that Reality Labs lost $19.19 billion and that capex is rising, but the filing states that RL's investments are funded by 'generating sufficient profits from other areas of our business,' and FoA profit of $102.47 billion covers that loss more than five times. Daily active people reached 3.58 billion, up 7%. The filing also says that 'our ongoing improvements to ad targeting and measurement are continuing to drive improved results for advertisers,' which supports the pricing gains. The risks are real and disclosed, but the reported growth and cash generation are strong.

claims.claim: Total 2025 revenue grew 22%, driven mainly by advertising.
claims.quote: Total revenue for 2025 was $200.97 billion, an increase of 22% compared to 2024, due to an increase in advertising revenue.

claims.claim: Operating cash flow reached a record level that funds the business.
claims.quote: The increase was due to $115.80 billion of cash generated from operations

claims.claim: Management says ad improvements are driving better advertiser results, supporting pricing.
claims.quote: We believe our ongoing improvements to ad targeting and measurement are continuing to drive improved results for advertisers.

bear.argument: The opponent's strongest points are real, but they do not settle the investment question. FoA profit of $102.47 billion does cover the $19.19 billion RL loss, yet the filing says RL's ability to continue depends on that coverage, and the RL loss is expected to recur in 2026. Revenue growth is also less durable than it looks. Ad impressions rose 12% and price per ad rose 9%, but management attributes the pricing gain to targeting tools whose signals it says are shrinking, and it warns that the same tools 'will continue to adversely impact' ad revenue. Free cash flow fell to $43.59 billion from $52.10 billion, and 2026 capex is guided to $115 to $135 billion, so the $31.57 billion returned to shareholders in 2025 is funded from a cash pool that is shrinking relative to spending. Net income fell to $60.46 billion from $62.36 billion, and the effective tax rate rose to 30%. Daily active people grew 7%, but the filing admits the count carries roughly 3% error. Set against these facts, the reported growth does not make the stock a safe holding.

claims.claim: Free cash flow fell despite higher operating cash flow
Capital spending guidance rises sharply for 2026
claims.quote: We anticipate making capital expenditures of approximately $115 billion to $135 billion in 2026 to support our AI efforts and core business

claims.claim: Management says ad-targeting changes will continue to hurt ad revenue
claims.quote: will continue to adversely impact our advertising revenue for the foreseeable future

bull.argument: The bear case is right that these risks exist, but the filing supports a more balanced reading. On cash, FCF fell to $43.59 billion from $52.10 billion only because capex rose to $69.69 billion of property purchases, and the company still produced $115.80 billion of operating cash flow, up from $91.33 billion. Cash and marketable securities rose $3.78 billion to $81.59 billion, even after $31.57 billion of buybacks and dividends, and $29.91 billion of net note proceeds. The filing does not describe a shrinking cash pool. On earnings, the 2025 net income dip came mainly from a $15.93 billion tax charge tied to OBBBA. Absent the valuation allowance, the effective tax rate would have been 13%, so pre-tax income rose from $70.66 billion to $85.93 billion. On pricing, the filing attributes the 9% rise in average price per ad to 'ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools,' and reports ad revenue up 22%. Reality Labs' loss is disclosed and bounded at roughly $19 billion against $102.47 billion of FoA operating income.

claims.claim: Operating cash flow rose sharply, and cash and marketable securities still increased in 2025.
claims.quote: Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $81.59 billion as of December 31, 2025, an increase of $3.78 billion from December 31, 2024.

claims.claim: The 2025 effective tax rate spike was driven by a one-time OBBBA charge, not core operations.
claims.quote: Absent the valuation allowance charge as of the enactment date, our 2025 effective tax rate would have decreased by 17 percentage points to 13%.

claims.claim: The filing attributes the pricing gain to ad performance from targeting and measurement tools.
claims.quote: The increase in average price per ad in 2025 was driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools.

judge.reasoning: Bull's cited quotes all verified and it directly rebutted the bear's tax and cash-pool points with the filing's own figures, including the ex-valuation-allowance tax rate and the rise in cash and securities. Bear's round-2 case leans on unverified claims (RL coverage dependence, shrinking signals, a 3% DAP error) and misattributes the 'will continue to adversely impact' language, which refers to legislative, regulatory and platform developments rather than the targeting tools. Bear's FCF point is valid, but it does not fully answer the bull's cash-generation rebuttal.
